title: A quantum optical concept of attosecond pulses: the attoquants
abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) is conventionally understood to produce attosecond pulse trains only when the emitted harmonics are mutually phase-locked, in accordance with the classical theory of mode-locking. Such locking is necessary for pulse synthesis when the harmonic field is in a separable multimode quantum state. This requirement, however, can be circumvented entirely for harmonic combs exhibiting intermodal entanglement. We introduce a novel family of multimode quantum states, termed attoquants: states associated with highly structured pulse trains that are inherently insensitive to relative phases. As a concrete example, we analyse the coherent permanent state, constructed as a completely symmetric superposition of products of coherent states over all permutations of a fixed parameter set. It is shown analytically that its electric-field expectation value is a locked Fourier superposition of the driving-field harmonics, yielding an attosecond pulse train without requiring mode-locking. We further calculate the photon statistics, the Wigner function, and the logarithmic negativity of this state, confirming it to be genuinely nonclassical and entangled. Finally, we offer a phenomenological interpretation for the generation of such entangled states during HHG, as a consequence of multi-atom effects. Since the coherence volume of the driving field greatly exceeds that of its harmonics, a collectively-driven cluster of atoms can radiate the individual harmonics as spatially resolved, but fundamentally indistinguishable sources. This can generate the permutation-symmetric entanglement structure of an attoquant.
summary: This paper proposes 'attoquants,' a new quantum state concept, to explain attosecond pulse generation in High-Harmonic Generation (HHG) without relying on the classical requirement of phase-locking. By analyzing the coherent permanent state, the authors prove that this entangled state inherently supports pulse trains. This offers a quantum-mechanical framework for understanding ultrafast light sources driven by collective atomic effects.
main_problem: To develop a quantum optical concept for attosecond pulse generation that bypasses the classical requirement of mutual phase-locking among emitted harmonics.
main_result: The authors introduce 'attoquants,' a novel class of multimode quantum states, demonstrating that their electric-field expectation value yields an attosecond pulse train without requiring mode-locking.
method: The analysis involves constructing and characterizing the coherent permanent state (an attoquant) and calculating quantum diagnostics like photon statistics and logarithmic negativity.
model_or_system: The system is High-Harmonic Generation (HHG), modeled quantum mechanically as a harmonic radiation field composed of quantized electromagnetic modes. The core theoretical tool is the attoquant state, which is a permutation-symmetric superposition of coherent states.
key_observables: Electric-field expectation value, photon statistics, Wigner function, and logarithmic negativity.
important_parameters: The structure of the harmonic field (discrete frequencies $(2q+1)\omega$) and the concept of intermodal entanglement.
main_assumptions: The analysis is theoretical, offering a phenomenological interpretation for the physical origin of these entangled states based on multi-atom effects during HHG.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the electric-field distribution for different pulse synthesis methods (mean-field vs. field-variance) and compare the temporal structure of field intensity for mode-locked versus random phase states.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the classical limitations of HHG to introducing the quantum attoquant concept, analytically deriving its properties, and finally providing a physical interpretation rooted in collective multi-atom radiation.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges quantum optics and attosecond physics by proposing a fundamentally quantum mechanism (entanglement) to achieve pulse synthesis, moving beyond semi-classical approximations.

Illustration of the electric-field distribution within (a) a purely mean-field pulse, (b) a purely field-variance pulse, and (c) a general pulse, in which the field-variance maximum coincides with the field-average maximum. The classical value of the electric field is shown as a dashed line in each panel.

Figure 2. (a) Temporal structure of ⟨ˆE⟩2 in units of E2 0, resulting from semiclassical states [equation (9)]. One can compare the cases of mode-locked (red) and random-phase (blue) conditions. (b) Coherent state parameters of the constituent coherent states in the complex plane, for the mode-locked (red) and random-phase (blue) cases. Here M=30 harmonics (5th to 63rd) of identical harmonic energies are used, with |αn| = 1 √3+2n .

Figure 3. (a) Temporal structure of (∆ˆE)2 in units of E2 0, resulting from a product of squeezed-vacuum states [equation (12)]. One can compare the cases of mode-locked (red) and random-phase (blue) conditions. The dashed green line indicates the corresponding vacuum variance. (b) Complex squeezing parameters of the constituent squeezed-vacuum states in the complex plane, for the mode-locked (red) and random-phase (blue) cases, respectively. Here M=30 harmonics (5th to 63rd) of identical harmonic energies are used, with rn = arsinh 2.1 √2n0+1+2n .

Figure 4. The photon statistics for {βk = 5 + δk} parameters, shown on the inset of each subfigure. (a)-(c) correspond to δk evenly distributed on a unit circle, with M=3, 4 and 12 modes, respectively. (d) corresponds to randomly distributed δk, with M=12 modes.

Figure 5. The photon statistics for {βk} parameters, distributed uniformly on a circle of modulus |βk| = 2 (a), |βk| = 4 (b), and |βk| = 8 (c). The corresponding Poissonian distribution is shown with black markers.
